turns.t: Welcome back, Ms. Delgado. I'm looking at the notes from your last visit, the one where we began treating your overactive thyroid. How have things been since then?
Better, I think? But I'm worried it isn't working as fast as it should. My heart is still racing sometimes.
Tell me more about the racing. How often does it happen?
A few times a week. Usually at night when I'm sitting down, which seems strange. Shouldn't it happen when I'm active?
Not necessarily. Too much thyroid hormone can stir up the heart even at rest. Does an episode last long?
Maybe ten minutes. I count the seconds, which probably makes it worse.
That's very understandable. And what about being hot all the time, which you described before? How's that?
Gone, honestly. It settled after the second week. I stopped sleeping with the window wide open.
That's a useful sign. Any chest pain when your heart races?
No. Just the pounding. Should I be worried it's my heart?
Let me finish my questions and I'll answer that properly. First, any double vision or discomfort in your eyes?
No, my eyes are fine, thank goodness.
Good. Now let's go through your medicines. Start with the thyroid one.
Methimazole. I think it's maybe 20 milligrams? Once a day, in the morning. I'd have to check the bottle.
That's okay, we'll confirm it against the pharmacy record. What else do you take?
Propranolol, 40 milligrams twice a day, for the racing heart. And a multivitamin once a day.
Any allergies to medicines or anything else?
No, none that I know of.
And besides the thyroid, any other medical problems I should know about?
The Graves' disease, that's what they called it. And high blood pressure, but that's mild.
Okay. Hold both hands out in front of you, fingers spread, and close your eyes.
I can see a fine tremor in both hands. Eyes open now.
Oh. I didn't even notice that. Is that normal?
It fits with your thyroid hormone still running a little high. Let me explain why, because it matters for what we do next.
Please do. I read online that this medicine can take months.
It can, and here's the reason. Your thyroid has a store of hormone already made. Methimazole stops new hormone being made, but the old stock has to be used up first, so improvement is gradual.
So the medicine is working, just slowly?

From what you've told me, I think your thyroid is still a bit overactive, but heading in the right direction. The hot feeling going away is part of that, and the racing is the thyroid hormone pushing on the heart, not damage to it.
Should I be taking more of it, then?
Not today. Changing a dose without a fresh blood test is guessing. I'd like to repeat the thyroid blood test in about four weeks, and then decide with real numbers.
Four weeks feels so long. What if the racing gets worse?
Then ring the clinic and tell them, don't wait for the test. That's what the number is for.
Okay. Is there anything I can do at night to calm it down?
Cut out coffee and tea after lunch, and try slow breathing when it starts. It won't cure it, but it helps some people feel more in control.
I do drink a lot of tea. My mother says it's the only thing keeping me going.
Switch to decaf in the afternoon and see how you feel. Small changes add up.
All right. I'll try that. I'm sorry for so many questions.
Please never apologize for those. They're exactly what I want to hear.
Thank you, doctor. I feel a bit calmer now.
Good. Keep taking everything as you have been, and ring if you need us.
